fields.description: Which API the model is called through. `openai` covers every OpenAI-compatible endpoint — OpenRouter, OpenAI, Groq, vLLM, LM Studio.
fields.label: Provider

fields.description: The API's base URL, without the trailing path.
fields.label: Base URL

fields.description: The model id, exactly as the provider knows it.
fields.label: Model

fields.description: Options for the provider that the app has no field for, as a JSON object — for example {"setCacheKey": "True"}. They are added to the request the app sends. A string that spells true or false becomes the boolean it means; the app's own settings are never overwritten by them.
fields.label: Extra Options

fields.description: The provider's API key. Stored encrypted; it is never sent to the browser and never written to a log.
fields.label: API Key

fields.description: Calls the provider with the smallest question that means anything, and says what happened. The values in this form are used, so a provider can be tested before it is saved.
fields.label: Test the connection

fields.description: Lower is more literal. Keep it low for a tool-using assistant: a high temperature turns a schema into a guess.
fields.label: Temperature

fields.description: The largest answer the model may produce, in tokens. Generous on purpose: a ceiling that cuts an answer off mid-sentence makes the assistant look as though it has run out of words. Lower it only if a provider refuses a request as too expensive.
fields.label: Max Tokens

fields.description: How long a single provider call may take, in seconds.
fields.label: Timeout (s)

fields.description: When the primary provider fails, try this one before giving up. A fallback on a different vendor is worth much more than one on the same vendor.
fields.label: Enable Fallback

fields.description: Which API the fallback is called through. The same three choices as the primary.
fields.label: Fallback Provider

fields.description: The fallback's base URL, without the trailing path.
fields.label: Fallback Base URL

fields.description: The fallback's model id, exactly as the provider knows it.
fields.label: Fallback Model

fields.description: The fallback's API key. Stored the same way as the primary's: encrypted, and never sent to the browser.
fields.label: Fallback API Key

fields.description: Whether the side chat is on at all, and where it sits on the Desk.
fields.label: The widget

fields.description: Turn the side chat off site-wide. The widget still renders in its locked state so the reason is visible rather than mysterious.
fields.label: Enabled

fields.description: Where the side-chat widget sits on the Desk. 'floating' overlays a helpdesk-style bubble instead of docking beside the Desk.
fields.label: Widget Position

fields.description: What the assistant may do without asking, and what its users may attach to a question.
fields.label: Safety

fields.description: When on, the assistant asks for your approval before creating or changing a document. On by default.
fields.label: Confirm writes

fields.description: How long a write waits for the reader's approval before it is given up on. The reader sees this count down on the approval card.
fields.label: Approval wait (seconds)

fields.description: When on, write tools run their validation and report what they would do, but nothing is saved. Use it to test prompts or train users without touching data.
fields.label: Dry Run

fields.description: When on, users may attach a file to a question. Only models that can read the file's type will see it.
fields.label: Attachment Support

fields.description: The largest attachment that may be attached, in kilobytes.
fields.label: Max Attachment Size (KB)

fields.description: Tool names, separated by commas or line breaks — one per line is easiest to read. A name that is not one of this app's tools is refused when you save: a name that matches no tool hides nothing from the assistant, and a setting that looks right while hiding nothing is worse than an error. The tools are list_docs, get_doc, get_doctype_meta, run_report, create_doc, update_doc, bulk_update_doc, submit_doc, cancel_doc, amend_doc, delete_doc, ask_question.
fields.label: Disabled tools

fields.description: How long an unanswered question the assistant asked the reader stays pending before it is cancelled. Zero means never expire.
fields.label: Question expiry (hours)

fields.description: How many tool rounds one question may take. A backstop against a runaway loop, not a budget: the assistant answers with what it has found when it is reached, rather than apologising for stopping.
fields.label: Max Tool Rounds

fields.description: How many past messages are replayed to the model as context. Generous, so a long conversation does not make the assistant forget what it was told.
fields.label: History Limit

fields.description: How long one turn may run, in seconds.
fields.label: Turn Timeout (s)

fields.description: How many questions one person may ask per minute, per surface. 0 means no limit.
fields.label: Turns / Minute

fields.description: What a million tokens cost, in this site's currency. The chat prices a turn with it, so the ledger is in your currency and not in the provider's. Leave it at 0 and the cost is not known.
fields.label: Price per Million Tokens

fields.description: Optional. When this month's estimated cost reaches it, System Managers are warned in the usage dialog. Leave blank for no limit.
fields.label: Monthly budget

fields.description: Replaces the built-in instructions. Leave empty to use the defaults.
fields.label: System Prompt
